findings.text: The staging mailbox exposes four consecutive 32 bit registers reached through one mapping sized as count times register width, with control at byte zero, status at byte four, write data at byte eight and read data at byte twelve.
Control uses bit zero for abort and bit thirty one for go, status uses bit two for error and bit thirty one for ready, and response status uses bits zero one and two for success progress and error.
A load operation uses command value three and staging object value eleven combined with vendor identity and transfer length expressed in double words to form the mailbox header.
Each mailbox header and each response occupies eight bytes, and a single mailbox transaction is allowed up to ten seconds of one millisecond waits before being treated as timed out.
Default total size is defined as default payload plus header size, and extended header and entry sizes are defined by their respective record sizes.
Staging progress is tracked by a record holding the mapped base address plus total image length, current piece length, cumulative bytes offered, and current image offset.

Extended signature data consists of entries carrying signature plus flags plus checksum, grouped under a table header that stores entry count and checksum with reserved words followed by a flexible entry array.

Staging maps the mailbox, issues a reset, then alternates between offering the current image piece and asking hardware for the next offset until an end marker or budget exhaustion, finally unmapping and reporting the terminal status.
Each offered piece is limited to one page or the remaining tail, and the cumulative amount offered may reach at most twice the image length, beyond which the attempt fails with a message size error.
A request places a size bearing header first, then a load command header, then the raw image bytes, accounts the bytes, signals readiness through control, and blocks waiting for hardware completion.

A response is read as header plus offset plus status, requires an exact expected header, accepts only the all ones value as completion or otherwise an offset within the image, and treats a response error flag as a protocol failure.

Completion is detected by polling status once per millisecond, an explicit error indication takes precedence as an input output failure, absence of ready after the limit yields a timeout, otherwise success.
Every read from the read port is acknowledged by writing zero back to the same port, and a 64 bit header is assembled from a low word followed by a high word.
Chunk bytes are emitted as ordered single word stores to an uncached mapping, relying on arrival in program sequence so hardware can reconstruct ordering.

The parser walks concatenated images, validates sizes and sanity, keeps only entries newer than the running revision that match the processor and pass safety and minimum version policy, retaining the newest qualifying image.
An image is considered safe for late loading only when its header advertises a nonzero required minimum and the boot processor revision already meets that minimum.

Late loading is refused on a specific Broadwell server variant and stepping when per core cache exceeds 2621440 bytes and the current revision is below a documented threshold, directing users toward early loading.
Late firmware is requested directly under directory intel-ucode with a name encoding family model and stepping in hex, then parsed as a linear byte stream before releasing the firmware object.
On success the pending late image becomes the retained global image after freeing any prior image, on failure the pending image is freed, and the pending slot is always cleared.

Preparation clears the offline set, aborts if an offline primary thread is found or when offline helpers are not permitted, records allowed offline helpers, and otherwise assigns each online processor a control processor derived from its sibling set with an initial wait state.

After preparation, a new image triggers an update through stopped processors with a safety flag reflecting the safety verdict, a missing image reports not found, an already current image reports success, and unexpected states report a bad descriptor.
A sysfs store accepts only the decimal value one, rejecting other input, and under protection performs the locked late load sequence, returning the input length on success.

Per processor entries expose revision and feature flags as hexadecimal text under a group named microcode, while the processor root group of the same name exposes a reload entry when late loading is configured.

Online arrival clears per processor state, collects the processor signature, publishes the revision including to boot state on processor zero, and creates the per processor group, while offline preparation invokes vendor cleanup and removes that group.
Boot processor resume reapplies a retained image when present and otherwise reloads the early image, exposed as a syscore resume callback through a registered syscore object.

Intel initialization rejects non Intel vendors, family below six and a legacy 64 bit variant, enables staging when architectural enumeration advertises it, computes per core cache size, and returns the Intel operation table, with header fallbacks returning null when support is absent.

Early initialization aborts when loading is disabled or the vendor lacks support, logs current and early updated revisions, creates a faux device and root group, then registers syscore handling and hotplug callbacks for online and offline transitions.

Late application must execute on the targeted processor itself, delegates to the low level apply helper, and on update or already current outcomes publishes the new revision to per processor and boot state as appropriate.

Built in handling proceeds only when a sentinel marks that the boot processor image was loaded, the loader is enabled and the vendor matches, then duplicates the discovered blob into retained storage when found.
The reload entry holds the CPUs read lock across the entire locked late load, preventing concurrent processor set changes during preparation and update.

Hardware may request the same piece repeatedly within the double length budget, reset is issued without waiting for status, malformed headers or out of range offsets are logged once and abort staging, and unresponsive hardware surfaces as timeout after the full wait.
Truncated headers, undersized totals, truncated payloads, allocation failures and sanity failures all abandon parsing, release temporary and candidate buffers, and report a generic update error.

The diagnostic prefix is the word microcode followed by colon and space, the built in location is the kernel x86 microcode directory path ending in GenuineIntel binary, and boot loaded state is marked by numeric value one used as a pointer sentinel.
The retained virtual image pointer plus pending late image pointer use read mostly placement while per core cache size uses post init read only placement to reflect rare updates.
